findings.title: Direct dependency rsa 0.9.10 ships with open timing side-channel advisory RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin Attack), permanently ignored
findings.description: rsa = "0.9" is a DIRECT workspace dependency (root Cargo.toml line 1886, consumed by crates/buff-crypto-extras for the Buff-visible RSA.* surface: RsaPrivateKey::new, to_pkcs8_pem, pkcs1v15 SigningKey/VerifyingKey sign/verify). Cargo.lock confirms a single resolved instance rsa 0.9.10. RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin Attack, timing side-channel key recovery) is in the cargo-audit hard gate's ignore list with the comment 'NO FIX AVAILABLE... Tracked in DR-019'. Unlike the other 23 ignores which are transitive/unmaintained notices, this is a cryptographic-vulnerability advisory on a first-party-declared dep that the workspace builds into every artifact.
findings.root_cause: Upstream RustCrypto has not patched Marvin for the 0.9 line; the project accepted the risk via DR-019 and suppressed the advisory rather than isolating or replacing the primitive.
findings.impact: Any Buff program using RSA.* via buff-crypto-extras links vulnerable code. Documented exposure is limited to sign/verify (no decryption lowering found in the root Cargo.toml T49 comment), which reduces but does not eliminate Marvin-class risk; the ignore is indefinite with no re-review trigger.
findings.recommendation: Keep the ignore but convert the indefinite suppression into a tracked, time-boxed decision: (1) add an expiry/re-review note to DR-019 and a comment in audit.toml naming the DR file path; (2) evaluate gating buff-crypto-extras RSA.sign behind an explicit opt-in or switching the signature surface to ed25519-dalek (already workspace-pinned for buff-audit) as the documented default; (3) watch for a fixed rsa release (0.9.x patch or 1.0) and bump immediately.

fix_examples.before:
# rsa 0.9.10 - direct workspace dep (rsa = "0.9"). NO FIX AVAILABLE.
# RUSTSEC-2023-0071: Marvin Attack (timing sidechannel key recovery).
# Upstream has not released a fix. Tracked in DR-019.
"RUSTSEC-2023-0071",
fix_examples.after:
# rsa 0.9.10 - direct workspace dep (rsa = "0.9"). NO FIX AVAILABLE.
# RUSTSEC-2023-0071: Marvin Attack (timing sidechannel key recovery).
# Upstream has not released a fix. ACCEPTED DEBT: .sisyphus/decisions/DR-019-rsa-marvin.md
# RE-REVIEW BY: 2027-01-10 (quarterly) or on any rsa 0.9.x/1.x release.
"RUSTSEC-2023-0071",

findings.fix_guide: 1) Locate the DR-019 record under .sisyphus/decisions/ (or create it if DR-019 is only referenced informally). 2) Add re-review cadence + replacement criteria (ed25519 default, RSA as opt-in). 3) Update the audit.toml ignore comment to point at the DR file so the rationale is discoverable from the gate failure path. 4) Add 'rsa RUSTSEC-2023-0071' to any release-checklist doc so major bumps re-run the decision. 5) cargo test -p buff-crypto-extras after any rsa bump.

effort_estimate.breakdown: triage+DR update 60m; upstream/release-watch setup 30m; ed25519-default evaluation spike 90m; doc+CI touch-ups 60m

confidence.rationale: Advisory presence, direct-dep status, and single locked version all verified from audit.toml, root Cargo.toml, and Cargo.lock. Exposure limited to sign/verify per documented API surface, which is why severity is high not critical.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: The pin itself is documented (DR-019) so it is exempt under the FP rule as a 'deliberate pin' ONLY where it carries no real risk; a crypto side-channel advisory on a direct dep is real risk, which the FP rule explicitly carves out. Finding attacks the unbounded ignore + missing re-review trigger, not the pin choice.

findings.title: quick-xml direct pin 0.37.5 sits below the RUSTSEC-2026-0194/0195 fix line (>=0.41.0) while the ignore rationale mislabels it 'transitive'
findings.description: Cargo.lock resolves FOUR quick-xml instances: 0.26.0, 0.37.5, 0.40.1, 0.41.0. The 0.37.5 instance is the workspace's DIRECT pin (root Cargo.toml line 862, quick-xml = "0.37", consumed by crates/buff-xml/Cargo.toml line 26 which parses user-supplied XML). audit.toml ignores RUSTSEC-2026-0194 (quadratic run time) and RUSTSEC-2026-0195 (unbounded namespace allocation) with the comment 'transitive dep, fix = upgrade to >=0.41.0' - but for the direct instance a fix IS available (bump the pin to 0.41), and the ignore comment mischaracterizes it as transitive. 0.41.0 already exists in the lock graph, proving ecosystem compatibility.
findings.root_cause: The ignore entry was written against the transitive quick-xml consumers and never revisited when quick-xml became a direct buff-xml dependency in T50.
findings.impact: DoS-class advisories (quadratic CPU, unbounded memory) on XML input parsing remain active in buff-xml; the hard-gate audit will never flag the direct instance because both advisories are blanket-ignored, and the stale rationale hides a one-line remediation.
findings.recommendation: Bump quick-xml = "0.37" to "0.41" at the workspace level, fix any 0.37-to-0.41 API drift in crates/buff-xml/src (Reader/Event API is stable across the range), then narrow the audit.toml ignore comments to name only the genuine transitive instances (0.26.0/0.40.1) or remove the ignores entirely once the resolved minimum reaches 0.41.
findings.fix_guide: 1) Edit root Cargo.toml line 862: quick-xml = "0.41". 2) cargo check -p buff-xml and cargo test -p buff-xml; fix any API drift in src/lib.rs (Reader::from_str / read_event_into / Event enum are stable 0.36-0.41 per the root pin comment). 3) Re-run Select-String on Cargo.lock: the buff-xml instance should resolve to 0.41.x. 4) Update .cargo/audit.toml lines 17-20: reword to 'transitive instances <0.41 only' and verify the audit_toml_reasons test still passes. 5) Update the pin-rationale comment (0.37 -> 0.41, released with the security fixes).

effort_estimate.breakdown: bump 5m; API-drift fix+tests 25m; audit.toml + comment updates 10m; cargo tree duplicate check 5m

confidence.rationale: Four lock instances, the 0.37.5 direct instance, the >=0.41 fix line, and the 'transitive' mislabel are all directly verified. Residual uncertainty: whether 0.37.5 specifically falls inside both advisory version ranges (assumed yes per the audit.toml's own fix statement '> =0.41.0').

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Not a documented deliberate pin: the conservative-pin philosophy covers staying on long-standing majors, but the repo's own audit ignore text concedes the fix is 'upgrade to >=0.41.0' - an available upgrade not taken, plus a factually wrong 'transitive' rationale. 0.41.0 is already resolved elsewhere in the lock, so the bump is ecosystem-proven.

findings.title: nalgebra workspace pin has zero consumers while root comment, crate AGENTS.md, and README all claim buff-science actively uses it
findings.description: Root Cargo.toml declares nalgebra = "0.33" (line 756) with a 10-line comment (lines 747-756) stating it is 'Used by buff-science for matrix inverse, determinant, solve, and LU decomposition' and listing the exact API surface (DMatrix::from_row_slice / Matrix::try_inverse / determinant / solve / transpose). Verified: NO crate manifest in the 73-crate workspace declares nalgebra (.workspace = true); crates/buff-science/Cargo.toml depends only on buff-tensor + thiserror + rayon; grep for 'nalgebra' across crates/buff-science/src returns zero matches; the manifest's own description says it uses 'pure-Rust Gauss-Jordan / LU' instead. buff-science's AGENTS.md DEPS section ('nalgebra (workspace 0.33) - DMatrix for inverse/determinant/solve') and README ('inverse(m) | nalgebra::DMatrix::try_inverse') are both wrong. Additionally the ndarray T8 comment block immediately below contains the second documented forward-pin rationale, so this pin looks deliberate but its documented consumer contract is false.
findings.root_cause: T13 implementation diverged from its spec: nalgebra delegation was replaced by hand-rolled linalg, but the root pin, the root comment, and both per-crate docs were never reconciled.
findings.impact: Dead workspace metadata plus three documents that will misdirect any contributor: a developer extending buff-science per AGENTS.md will assume nalgebra is wired and DMatrix-backed (numerically pivoted LU), while the actual hand-rolled Gauss-Jordan may have different numerical-stability properties than documented. It also inflates the apparent dependency surface of the 'pure-Rust' matrix story.
findings.recommendation: Pick one and execute: (A) honor the docs - add nalgebra.workspace = true to crates/buff-science/Cargo.toml and delegate inverse/determinant/solve to DMatrix as documented; or (B) honor the code - delete the nalgebra pin + comment from root Cargo.toml and correct crates/buff-science/AGENTS.md + README.md to describe the hand-rolled implementation. Given the AGENTS.md 'WHY nalgebra' section argues pivoted LU for numerical stability, option A is the stronger fix; option B is the minimal one.

fix_examples.before:
[dependencies]
# T13: buff-tensor for the primary Tensor<f32> matrix type.
buff-tensor.workspace = true
fix_examples.after:
[dependencies]
# T13: buff-tensor for the primary Tensor<f32> matrix type.
buff-tensor.workspace = true
# T13: nalgebra DMatrix for inverse/determinant/solve (pivoted LU).
nalgebra.workspace = true

findings.fix_guide: Option A: 1) Add 'nalgebra.workspace = true' to crates/buff-science/Cargo.toml [dependencies]. 2) Rewrite src/linalg.rs inverse/determinant/solve to wrap DMatrix::from_row_slice + try_inverse/determinant/solve per the documented API. 3) cargo test -p buff-science (15+ unit tests incl. proptest roundtrips are the safety net). Option B: 1) Delete root Cargo.toml lines 747-756. 2) Fix crates/buff-science/AGENTS.md (DEPS + WHY-nalgebra sections) and README.md API table. 3) Remove 'Audit nalgebra extern surface' row from the WHERE-TO-LOOK table.

effort_estimate.breakdown: docs-fix path: root comment removal 10m, AGENTS.md+README 30m, verification 20m; wiring path: dep add 10m, linalg rewrite 150m, tests 80m

detection_method.query: foreach key in workspace.dependencies: Get-ChildItem crates -Filter Cargo.toml -Recurse | Select-String -Pattern ('^\\s*' + key + '(\\s*=|\\.workspace\\s*=)') ; grep pattern 'nalgebra' in crates/buff-science/src

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path Cargo.toml -Pattern '^nalgebra'; Get-ChildItem crates -Filter Cargo.toml -Recurse | Select-String -Pattern '^\s*nalgebra(\s*=|\.workspace\s*=?=?)'; Select-String -Path crates\buff-science\Cargo.toml -Pattern 'nalgebra'; Select-String -Path crates\buff-science\src\*.rs -Pattern 'nalgebra'

confidence.rationale: Zero-consumer status proven by exhaustive manifest scan (73 manifests, dot-syntax pattern validated against known-good consumers like jsonwebtoken.workspace) plus zero source references. Comment-vs-code mismatch quoted verbatim from four documents.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Documented forward-pins are FP-exempt, but this is not a forward-pin: the comment asserts PRESENT-TENSE active consumption ('Used by buff-science', API surface listed) that is provably false in code and manifest. The finding is the doc/code contract break, not the pin's existence.

findings.title: reqwest_011 alias pin is dead: zero consumers, and its T48-fix rationale claims buff-web3 calls reqwest_011::Client::new() which it does not
findings.description: Root Cargo.toml line 511 declares reqwest_011 = { package = "reqwest", version = "0.11", ... } with a 7-line rationale (lines 504-511) stating 'To let buff-web3 (T48) call Http::new(reqwest_011::Client::new()) for its panic-free Provider::default fallback, we expose reqwest 0.11 under the alias reqwest_011'. Verified: no manifest in the workspace declares reqwest_011 (.workspace = true); grep for 'reqwest_011' across crates/buff-web3/src returns zero matches; crates/buff-web3/Cargo.toml (lines 53-70) explicitly lists the crates lib.rs 'uses directly' - serde_json, hex, rand_08, url - and reqwest_011 is not among them. The T48-fix pattern did land for rand_08 (which HAS a consumer) but not for reqwest_011. buff-web3 reaches reqwest 0.11 only transitively through ethers.
findings.root_cause: buff-web3's implementation evolved (Provider fallback via ethers' Http + catch_unwind, per crates/buff-web3/AGENTS.md) and dropped the direct reqwest_011 usage, but the workspace alias pin and its rationale comment were left behind.
findings.impact: Inert workspace metadata that keeps reqwest 0.11 (an EOL major with the documented h2 0.3 advisory chain, see .sisyphus/decisions/accepted-debt-ethers-oauth2.md and RUSTSEC-2026-0258 ignore) looking like a deliberately direct-supported surface. A future reader may 'safely' build against reqwest_011 believing it maintained, or cargo-deny/maintenance reviews waste time re-deriving its purpose.
findings.recommendation: Delete the reqwest_011 pin and its comment block (root Cargo.toml lines 504-511). The transitive reqwest 0.11 via ethers is unaffected - pins are only meaningful for direct manifest consumers. If the T48-fix alias pattern is worth preserving as documentation, fold one sentence into the existing accepted-debt DR instead.

fix_examples.before:
# T48-fix: ethers 2.0.14 internally pins `reqwest` to 0.11 (its
# `Http::new(reqwest::Client)` ctor expects the 0.11 type). The workspace
# `reqwest = "0.12"` (above) is API-incompatible. To let `buff-web3` (T48)
# call `Http::new(reqwest_011::Client::new())` for its panic-free
# `Provider::default` fallback, we expose reqwest 0.11 under the alias
# `reqwest_011`. Both versions coexist (ethers pulls 0.11 transitively).
# Pure-Rust via the `rustls-tls` feature (no native-tls, no cc-rs).
reqwest_011 = { package = "reqwest", version = "0.11", default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls-tls"] }
fix_examples.after:
# T48 note: buff-web3 consumes reqwest 0.11 ONLY transitively via ethers 2
# (no direct alias pin - the earlier reqwest_011 alias was removed when
# Provider::default stopped constructing its own client). See
# .sisyphus/decisions/accepted-debt-ethers-oauth2.md for the 0.11-line debt.

findings.fix_guide: 1) Remove line 511 and comment lines 504-510 from root Cargo.toml. 2) cargo check --workspace to confirm resolution (no manifest references it, so removal is inert). 3) Optionally add the one-sentence note above so the ethers->reqwest-0.11 chain stays discoverable from the root file. 4) Re-run the conventions validator: ./scripts/check-conventions.ps1.

detection_method.query: Get-ChildItem crates -Filter Cargo.toml -Recurse | Select-String -Pattern 'reqwest_011' ; grep pattern 'reqwest_011' in crates/buff-web3/src/*.rs

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path Cargo.toml -Pattern 'reqwest_011'; Get-ChildItem crates -Filter Cargo.toml -Recurse | Select-String -Pattern 'reqwest_011'; Get-ChildItem crates\buff-web3 -Recurse -Include *.rs | Select-String -Pattern 'reqwest_011'

confidence.rationale: Triple-verified: zero manifest consumers (validated scan methodology), zero source references in the claimed consumer crate, and the claimed consumer's manifest explicitly enumerates its direct deps without reqwest_011. rand_08 sibling pin having a live consumer confirms the scan detects the dot-syntax correctly.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Forward-pin rationale ('so a future consumer can reuse') would be FP-exempt, but this pin's own comment claims a PRESENT consumer by name and call-site, which is verifiably false. The finding targets the stale claim and dead metadata, not a deliberate conservative pin.

findings.title: Toolchain and checkout actions use mutable major-tag refs while all sibling actions are SHA-pinned; AGENTS.md still claims CI uses unpinned @master
findings.description: ci.yml (7 occurrences: lines 65, 97, 128, 150, 165, 280, 318) and security.yml (lines 23, 54) reference dtolnay/rust-toolchain@v1 and actions/checkout@v4 (also 11 occurrences) - mutable major tags that can be retargeted upstream. Every OTHER third-party action in these workflows IS commit-SHA-pinned with a version comment: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@3c63498..., Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b49..., docker/setup-buildx@8d2750c..., docker/build-push-action@ca052bb..., actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8..., softprops/action-gh-release@3bb1273.... Additionally AGENTS.md line 229 asserts '.github/workflows/ci.yml uses dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master' - stale; the actual ref is @v1, and rust-toolchain.toml/CI both agree on toolchain: 1.95.0, so the documented 'toolchain mismatch' risk is misdescribed while the real (smaller) mutable-ref exposure goes undocumented.
findings.root_cause: A hardening pass SHA-pinned the newer/less-common actions but left the two most common ones (checkout, rust-toolchain) on mutable tags; AGENTS.md was written against an older @master state and not updated after the move to @v1.
findings.impact: A upstream tag retarget or compromise of dtolnay/rust-toolchain or actions/checkout injects arbitrary code into every CI job that installs the toolchain - the highest-privilege step in the pipeline. Inconsistent pinning also undermines the audit trail the SHA-pinned actions were pinned for. The stale AGENTS.md note means contributors auditing supply-chain will look for a risk that no longer exists and miss the one that does.
findings.recommendation: Pin dtolnay/rust-toolchain and actions/checkout to full commit SHAs with '# v1' / '# v4' comments matching the existing house style (or adopt Dependabot/renovate with 'pin GitHub Actions' to maintain SHAs automatically). Then update AGENTS.md NOTES line 229 to state the @v1 + SHA-pin arrangement and drop the obsolete @master mismatch paragraph.

fix_examples.before:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4 # v4
- uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@v1
  with:
    toolchain: 1.95.0
    components: rustfmt
fix_examples.after:
- uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4
- uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain<sha-of-v1-tip> # v1
  with:
    toolchain: 1.95.0
    components: rustfmt

findings.fix_guide: 1) Resolve current SHAs: git ls-remote https://github.com/actions/checkout v4 and git ls-remote https://github.com/dtolnay/rust-toolchain v1 (or take them from the workflow run logs' 'Download action repository' lines). 2) Replace @v4/@v1 with @<sha> plus trailing '# v4'/'# v1' comments in ci.yml (11 + 7 spots) and security.yml (2 + 2 spots); release.yml/pages.yml/docker.yml if they use the same actions. 3) Update AGENTS.md line 229 to describe the SHA-pinned setup and delete the @master claim. 4) Optionally add .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem 'github-actions' + allow 'pinned' to keep SHAs fresh.

effort_estimate.breakdown: SHA resolution 10m; edit 4 workflow files 15m; AGENTS.md update 5m; verify one CI run 10m

detection_method.query: Select-String -Path .github\workflows\*.yml -Pattern 'uses: .*@'; compare SHA-pinned vs tag-pinned refs

references: C:\Users\vsbb1\source\repos\buff\.github\workflows\ci.yml lines 53-68 (contrast SHA-pinned cargo-deny-action line 54 vs checkout@v4 line 53/rust-toolchain@v1 line 65)

confidence.rationale: All refs enumerated directly from the workflow files; the inconsistency is mechanically verifiable. Severity held at medium because the toolchain VERSION itself is consistently 1.95.0 everywhere (no version drift), so exposure is limited to action-code supply chain, not toolchain-version surprises.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: The audit brief framed this as '@master unpinned major' - reality is @v1, which is still a mutable ref; either way the internal inconsistency against the repo's own SHA-pinning house style is objective, and the AGENTS.md staleness is quoted verbatim. No project convention endorses mutable tags for the already-SHA-pinned siblings.

findings.title: AGENTS.md dioxus caret-pin drift warning is obsolete: workspace uses exact =0.7.9 pins since T29, and no CI re-test guard exists or is needed
findings.description: AGENTS.md line 236 warns 'dioxus = "0.7" and dioxus-ssr = "0.7" are workspace caret pins... re-test on every minor bump'. Reality (root Cargo.toml lines 540-563): T29 (v1.25 tech-debt batch) upgraded both to EXACT pins dioxus = "=0.7.9" and dioxus-ssr = "=0.7.9" specifically 'to prevent surprise breakage from dioxus-rsx proc-macro changes'. The caret scenario the warning describes cannot occur - no minor bump can be resolved silently. The companion question from the audit scope ('is the re-test guard documented in CI?'): no dioxus-specific job exists in ci.yml; dioxus breakage would surface only via the clippy hard gate (compile-time) and the advisory continue-on-error test jobs.
findings.root_cause: T29 changed the pins but the AGENTS.md NOTES section (which the same T29-era edits touched elsewhere) kept the older caret-pin text.
findings.impact: Low: documentation overstates a risk that has been mitigated. Harm is indirect - reviewers may distrust the dependency story ('caret risk!') during audits/launch reviews, and the true residual risk (proc-macro behavior changes on a DELIBERATE manual bump of =0.7.9, caught only by advisory tests) is not stated anywhere actionable.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite AGENTS.md line 236 to: (a) state the exact =0.7.9 pins and their T29 rationale; (b) re-point the re-test obligation at MANUAL bumps - 'when bumping the =0.7.9 pins, run buff-ui-dioxus + ssr tests and the wasm build, since dioxus-rsx internals are not semver-covered'; (c) optionally note that ci.yml clippy is the only hard gate covering dioxus compile breakage.

fix_examples.before: - **Dioxus 0.7 version drift risk**: `dioxus = "0.7"` and `dioxus-ssr = "0.7"` are workspace caret pins. dioxus-rsx proc-macro internals are NOT covered by semver guarantees - re-test on every minor bump. See `.sisyphus/decisions/dioxus-feasibility.md` (T121b spike).
fix_examples.after: - **Dioxus 0.7 exact pins**: `dioxus = "=0.7.9"` and `dioxus-ssr = "=0.7.9"` (T29 exact pins - dioxus-rsx proc-macro internals are NOT covered by semver guarantees). When bumping the pin MANUALLY: re-run buff-ui-dioxus + `buff ssr` tests and the wasm32 build; ci.yml clippy is the only hard gate on compile breakage. See `.sisyphus/decisions/dioxus-feasibility.md` (T121b spike).

findings.fix_guide: 1) Edit AGENTS.md line 236 per the example. 2) Cross-check line 134/238 tier text while in the file (see AUD-DEP-007). 3) No code or CI change required; optionally add a comment at root Cargo.toml lines 556/563 pointing back at the refreshed NOTES entry.

confidence.rationale: Pin text quoted verbatim from both files; the exact-pin upgrade is self-documented in the root file's T29 comment, making the AGENTS.md staleness unambiguous.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: The underlying caret risk the audit brief asked about does NOT exist in code - reporting it as a dependency risk would itself be a false positive; the verified finding is the stale documentation, which is real and quotable. Doc drift is a genuine low-severity audit output, not a convention violation.

findings.title: AGENTS.md version-tier claim '1.2.0 (17 core compiler crates)' contradicts reality (8 crates) and its own line 238
findings.description: AGENTS.md line 134 states 'Three version tiers: 1.2.0 (17 core compiler crates), 1.0.0 (11 tooling crates...)'. Measured across crates/*/Cargo.toml: exactly 8 crates carry version = "1.2.0" (buff-lang-error/ast/lexer/parser/types/codegen-rust/codegen-wgsl/runtime) - the other 9 buff-lang-* crates (check, fmt, pipeline, debug-info, ffi-guide, ast-rsx, buffhtml-parser, codegen-buffhtml, cli) are at 1.0.0. AGENTS.md line 238 states the tier correctly ('1.2.0 for the core compiler crates (ast/lexer/parser/types/codegen-rust/codegen-wgsl/runtime/error)'), so the document contradicts itself, and the root Cargo.toml tier comment (lines 5-27) agrees with line 238. The conventions-lint CI job (scripts/check-conventions.ps1) enforces the per-crate tiers mechanically, so this is documentation-only.
findings.root_cause: The '17' figure counts all buff-lang-* crates (compiler-adjacent included) while the 1.2.0 tier only covers the 8 foundational pipeline crates; the line was written from crate-count instead of tier membership.
findings.impact: Cosmetic-to-moderate: contributors following line 134 would version a new core-adjacent crate (e.g. a new buff-lang-* crate) at 1.2.0 and have the conventions-lint reject it, or misjudge which crates need a coordinated tier bump at release time.
findings.recommendation: Change line 134 to '1.2.0 (8 core pipeline crates: error/ast/lexer/parser/types/codegen-rust/codegen-wgsl/runtime)' or simply reference line 238's enumeration so the two entries cannot diverge again.

fix_examples.before: - **Edition 2021, license `MIT OR Apache-2.0`**. Three version tiers: `1.2.0` (17 core compiler crates), `1.0.0` (11 tooling crates: ...) + 44 framework crates.
fix_examples.after: - **Edition 2021, license `MIT OR Apache-2.0`**. Three version tiers: `1.2.0` (8 core pipeline crates: error/ast/lexer/parser/types/codegen-rust/codegen-wgsl/runtime), `1.0.0` (tooling + remaining buff-lang-* crates + 44 framework crates).

findings.fix_guide: 1) Edit AGENTS.md line 134. 2) Verify: Get-ChildItem crates\*\Cargo.toml | Select-String '^version = "1\.2\.0"' | Measure-Object => 8. 3) No other file references the '17 crates' tier figure (grep to confirm before merging).
findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path AGENTS.md -Pattern '17 core'; (Get-ChildItem crates\*\Cargo.toml | Select-String -Pattern '^version = "1\.2\.0"' | Measure-Object).Count

confidence.rationale: Pure arithmetic: 8 manifests match version = "1.2.0"; the contradicting in-document line 238 is quoted; root Cargo.toml comment agrees with 238.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Zero-risk doc arithmetic error; no convention declares 17 crates at 1.2.0 and the enforcement script follows the real tiers, so the finding cannot be a misreading of a deliberate convention.

findings.title: ndarray T8 rationale comment block duplicated verbatim in workspace.dependencies (lines 762-780 and 785-803)
findings.description: The 19-line comment block beginning '# T8 (buff-tensor): the canonical Rust N-dimensional array crate.' (including the (a)/(b)/(c) forward-pin rationale and the 'Mirrors the chrono/tokio/regex codegen-only linking boundary' tail) appears TWICE back-to-back: lines 762-780 and lines 785-803, separated only by the one-line T9 note ('T9: buff-image and T11 buff-dsp workspace deps... are added by those sibling tasks downstream'). The ndarray key itself is declared once (line 781). The duplicate arose when the T9 note was spliced between a pasted copy of the block and the original.
findings.root_cause: Copy-paste splice error during the T9 comment insertion; the block was duplicated instead of the note being inserted between distinct comments.
findings.impact: None at build time (comments only). Documentation cost: the file is the project's canonical T-numbered rationale registry (AGENTS.md: 'add to root [workspace.dependencies] first (heavily documented)'); duplicated rationale invites divergent future edits and makes diff review of this hot-file noisier.
findings.recommendation: Delete the second occurrence (lines 785-803), keeping the T9 cross-reference note and the single ndarray comment + pin.

fix_examples.before:
# T9: `buff-image` and `buff-dsp` workspace deps (image, rustfft, realfft, apodize) are added by those sibling tasks downstream in
# this file - T8 does NOT duplicate them here.
# T8 (buff-tensor): the canonical Rust N-dimensional array crate.

findings.title: Documented 'reserved' crates-io/ directory does not exist on disk and no crates.io publish workflow exists despite README promising future crates.io installation
findings.description: AGENTS.md (STRUCTURE and NOTES) documents 'crates-io/ - EMPTY (reserved for future crates.io publishing)' and the anti-patterns list forbids populating it without coordination. Verified: Test-Path crates-io => False (the directory is not present on disk and not tracked). Additionally, README.md Option 5 tells users they can eventually 'cargo install buff-cli --locked' from crates.io, but .github/workflows contains no publish workflow: release.yml only builds 5-target binaries and publishes a GitHub Release (line 7 'publishes them to a GitHub Release', line 130 'Publish GitHub Release'); no 'cargo publish' / crates.io step exists in any workflow (ci/security/release/pages/docker/bufflings).
findings.root_cause: The reserved directory was never committed (empty dirs are not tracked by git without a placeholder), and crates.io publishing was deferred but the README future-tense and AGENTS.md reservation were left pointing at infrastructure that does not exist yet.
findings.impact: Cosmetic/coordination only: no build or release path breaks today. Risks are (a) contributors creating crates-io/ content per AGENTS.md will find the dir absent and may scatter files elsewhere; (b) when crates.io publishing day arrives, there is no scaffolded workflow and the README claim is unbacked; (c) the repo's OWN publishing story (dual-licensed, repository/keywords/categories metadata already present in every crate manifest - e.g. buff-web3 lines 13-15) implies publish-readiness that the pipeline does not deliver.
findings.recommendation: Add a placeholder to make the reservation real (crates-io/README.md with the reservation text + .gitkeep semantics), and either add a stub .github/workflows/publish.yml (manual_dispatch, requiring CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret, starting with a single low-risk crate such as buff-lang-error) or add one sentence to README Option 5 stating crates.io publishing is not yet available. Align AGENTS.md wording with whichever choice is made.

The remaining ~20 (rkyv RUSTSEC-2026-0235, async-std, fxhash, instant, paste, proc-macro-error, rustls-pemfile, unic-*, event-listener, webpki set) were read and confirmed documented, but their transitive consumer paths were not individually re-derived via cargo tree - deeper vulnerable-reachable-code analysis deferred.

The scripted scan found 35 workspace path pins (buff-dataframe, buff-audio, buff-dsp, buff-geo, etc.) consumed by no other manifest. All spot-checked ones carry the documented 'so any future consumer resolves to the same in-tree version' forward-registration rationale, so they were FP-exempted as a documented deliberate pattern rather than individually audited; if any lacks its root comment, it would be an additional finding.

deny.toml has no [sources] section, but CI invokes only 'cargo deny check bans licenses', so sources checking is out of scope of the existing gate by construction; judged not-a-gap under current CI wiring rather than a finding, but becomes one if 'check sources' is ever enabled without a config.

Version-tier consistency was verified from manifests + the root tier comment; a resolver-level confirmation (cargo metadata --no-deps / cargo check) was not executed, so a semver-incompatible cross-crate requirement introduced without a matching lock update would be missed by this text-level audit (conventions-lint CI claims coverage).

Root Cargo.toml documents accepted duplicates (windows-sys x5, hashbrown x5, tungstenite x4, darling x3, spin x3, quick-xml x4 discovered independently). Current duplicate inventory was NOT re-derived from Cargo.lock; new duplicates added since the debt-zero W4 audit would not be flagged.
